overview: White offers the b-pawn with 3.b4 after 1.g3 d5 2.Bg2 e5, aiming for Bb2 and pressure on e5 and d5 along the long diagonals. If Black takes with 3...Bxb4 White has a lead in development and diagonal pressure but is a pawn down; Black can also reply 3...e4 or 3...a5. A rare and risky surprise line.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Bb2 and Nf3 to hit e5
Use Bg2 pressure on d5 and open lines

black_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with ...Bxb4 and trade pieces

typical_structures.structure: Pawn centre d5/e5 for Black against White queenside pawn thrust

character.notes: White sacrifices a pawn for diagonal pressure, and the play gets tactical.

gambit.notes: Black can keep the b4 pawn.

soundness.notes: Considered an unsound surprise by most strong players.

structure.notes: The centre is open on the long diagonals and central pawns stay in contact.

level.notes: It is Dubious, so not a first repertoire choice.

character.reason: A pawn sacrifice early for long-diagonal pressure.

gambit.reason: White offers the b-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Black can take the pawn and hold it, so White has little to show.

structure.reason: Long diagonals and an open centre dominate; the d5/e5 pawns are in contact.

approach.reason: Seldom played at a high level.

level.reason: Dubious so never Beginner; some trap knowledge.

plans.reason: White's fianchettoed bishops aim down both long diagonals.
